newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Stark sees only few exceptions under budget rules.
newsitem.headline: Stark sees only few exceptions under budget rules.

text.p: The terms of the European Union's budget pact, although less strict than Germany might originally have liked, should still create only relatively few cases where exemption from fines would be granted, a German official said.
Juergen Stark, state secretary to the finance ministry, told Reuters that Bonn believed exemptions would only have been granted to EU nations in about 20 cases over the last 35 years.

Under the terms of the pact, a country is considered exempt from fines for running a high budget deficit if its economy shrinks by two percent within a year. It may argue it is a special case if its economy contracts by 0.75 percent or more, but must prove why this is so.

The European Union on Friday agreed the broad terms of a so-called stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline within monetary union. Those who overspend will face fines unless 'extraordinary and temporary circumstances' force spending up.

Germany, which first proposed the pact, has argued all along that the definitions of the economic circumstances which will allow excessive spending must be as strict as possible. It wanted no exemptions unless an economy shrank by two percent.

But Stark said Bonn did not believe the new rule would allow a much larger number of cases of overspending to occur without fines. "We think there would have been about 20 cases in the last 35 years within the current EU membership," he said.

"It is important to remember that not every case where an economy shrinks by 0.75 percent will be an exception," he added. "The onus lies with the country itself to prove that this was an exceptional circumstance."
Under the terms of the deal, nations agreed not to plead special economic circumstances unless their economies contracted by at least 0.75 percent.

Under its original proposal of a two percent contraction, Bonn estimated that there would have been 13 exceptional cases. A lower figure of a 1.5 percent contraction would have yielded about 15 cases.
